A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Video-R1 and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. All 12 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2 were inspected, including v2 Appendices A–E; v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original Video-R1 evaluations across six benchmarks, component ablations, training curves, and model-generated reasoning examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds 64-frame evaluations, longer RL training, additional ablations, and temporal-reasoning measurements.

M1.justification: Equation 1 changes temporal-reward eligibility from p > 0.8 times the shuffled-group accuracy to p >= the shuffled-group accuracy, eliminating mu. Section 3.3 increases the length-reward weight from 0.1 to 0.2. The architecture, mixed image/video training, and SFT-then-RL pipeline remain intact.

E1.justification: Training sources and all six quantitative benchmarks remain unchanged. A limited qualitative task-format change occurs in the MMVU energy example: v1 Figure 3 supplies multiple-choice options, whereas v2 Figure 9 presents an open-ended question and textual answer. This does not establish an expansion of the quantitative MMVU evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Video-R1-7B-zero, which omits the SFT cold start, and Figure 8 adds Video-R1-wo-len as a comparison variant. External baselines in Table 1 are retained; Kangeroo becoming Kangaroo is a spelling correction.

E3.justification: V2 adds 64-frame evaluation alongside the retained 16/32-frame settings and a separate 10k-step RL experiment alongside the original 1k-step experiment. Section 4.5 introduces Qwen2.5-VL-72B selection and judging of temporal-reasoning responses and an alpha sweep from 0.1 to 0.4. These substantially extend the evaluation design without replacing the original benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's image-data and temporal-training ablations, v2 tests the SFT cold start, length reward, temporal-reward sensitivity, and longer RL training. It also measures temporal-reasoning usage directly and adds an MVBench reasoning case. These additions investigate several previously untested components and mechanism claims.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The redrawn training curves do not introduce repeated-run uncertainty estimates; group reward normalization remains part of the algorithm.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 scores and the original Table 2 ablation scores are retained. V2 adds 64-frame results, including 37.1% VSI-Bench accuracy, rather than improving the retained 32-frame value of 35.8%. New results include 75.0% versus 60.2% temporal-reasoning usage and additional ablations. Table 3 reports mixed effects of longer training: at 64 frames, VSI-Bench rises from 37.1 to 37.8 while VideoMMMU falls from 52.4 to 51.4 between 1k and 10k steps.

T1.justification: The piecewise temporal-reward definition in Equation 1 changes its mathematical eligibility condition and removes mu. The normalized advantage and clipped policy objective remain mathematically equivalent under revised notation. No new theorem, proof, or formal guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 omits v1 Section 4.2's explicit claim to a new state of the art on VSI-Bench. The central Video-R1, T-GRPO, dataset, and GPT-4o-outperformance claims remain. The higher abstract accuracy reflects the added 64-frame setting rather than a broader methodological contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning the importance of SFT initialization, tolerance to temporal-reward magnitude, and length reward preserving deeper reasoning. Appendix E retains most earlier limitations but replaces the proposed future scaling experiment with discussion of dependence on handcrafted rewards and generalist reward modeling. Section 3.4 also softens explicit RL-emergence wording into a description of self-reflective capability.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D newly disclose training/inference and judging prompts, Adam with learning rate 1e-6, response-group sizes of 8 and 4, KL weight 0.04, gradient clipping, weight decay, maximum response length, and training times. V2 specifies Instruct model variants and reports up to eight A100 GPUs instead of four H20 GPUs. These substantially improve documentation; the code/data access location is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds eleven cited works, including Vision-R1, Logic-RL, VideoLLM-online, domain-specific RL work, and surveys. These broaden citation coverage without substantially changing the video-reasoning novelty position. The retitled self-improving cognition reference retains the same arXiv identifier and is not a new work.

P1.justification: The main section sequence is retained, with localized shortening of the self-reflection, setup, results, and training-curve discussions. Limitations move from Section 5 to Appendix E, and appendix cross-references are added. Author information, CoT capitalization, wording, and an erroneous table reference are also revised.

P2.justification: V2 adds a T-GRPO schematic, temporal-reasoning and sensitivity charts, length-reward plots, a scaling table, prompt-template displays, and an MVBench example. Figure 5 is redrawn with clearer axes and sampled trajectories; Tables 1–2 gain rows. The MMVU example moves to Appendix B with revised content, while the VSI-Bench example is retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's two ablations and sparse implementation details, v2 provides useful tests of cold-start and reward components plus substantial prompt and optimizer documentation. These improve empirical support and reproducibility. The gain remains limited because the reward-setting revisions are not reconciled with the retained benchmark scores, and the disclosed prompt already requests self-reflection, limiting what the examples establish about RL-induced 'aha moments'.
